headline: Spanish Frequent Verbs Foundation
threshold: Recognize and use sixty frequent spoken verbs, their everyday meanings, complements and regional cautions.

lessons.title: Identity and description
lessons.objective: Identity and description: Present ser identifies and describes; use estar for many states and locations.

words.en: I am a student of Spanish.

words.es: El curso es por la tarde.
words.en: The course is in the afternoon.

words.es: Somos seis personas en el grupo.
words.en: There are six of us in the group.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing identity and description. Present ser identifies and describes; use estar for many states and locations. Identity, origin and profession commonly use ser. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Saying and telling
lessons.objective: Saying and telling: Decir introduces words or a message.

words.en: I say my name when I enter.
What do you say when you do not understand?
We say that we need help.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing saying and telling. Decir introduces words or a message. Present digo / dices contrasts with preterite dije / dijiste. Decirle algo a alguien means tell someone something. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Location and temporary conditions
lessons.objective: Location and temporary conditions: Estar locates people and things and describes many conditions; events are often located with ser.

words.es: Los libros están sobre la mesa.
words.en: The books are on the table.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing location and temporary conditions. Estar locates people and things and describes many conditions; events are often located with ser. Use estoy / estás / está / estamos / están. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Possession and expressions
lessons.objective: Possession and expressions: Tener expresses possession, age and conditions such as hunger.

words.en: My brother is twenty years old.
Do you have time to eat?

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing possession and expressions. Tener expresses possession, age and conditions such as hunger. Tener que + infinitive expresses an obligation; present tengo but tienes / tiene. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Doing and making
lessons.objective: Doing and making: Hacer covers doing, making and many fixed expressions.

words.en: I do my homework at home.
What do you do after work?

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing doing and making. Hacer covers doing, making and many fixed expressions. Present hago is irregular; preterite hice / hizo differs from the present stem. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Auxiliary haber and hay
lessons.objective: Auxiliary haber and hay: Hay means there is / there are.

words.es: Hay una farmacia en esta calle.
words.en: There is a pharmacy on this street.

words.es: Hay dos personas en la entrada.
words.en: There are two people at the entrance.

words.es: No hay agua en la botella.
words.en: There is no water in the bottle.

words.es: He comprado pan para la cena.
words.en: I have bought bread for dinner.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing auxiliary haber and hay. Hay means there is / there are. Auxiliary haber combines with an invariant participle: he comido. Existential hay is not the same paradigm as auxiliary he / has / ha. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Going and planning
lessons.objective: Going and planning: Ir uses voy / vas / va / vamos / van.

words.en: I go to the market on foot.

words.es: Mi amiga va a la estación.
words.en: My friend goes to the station.
We are going to buy fruit.

words.es: Después voy a preparar la cena.
words.en: Afterward I am going to prepare dinner.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing going and planning. Ir uses voy / vas / va / vamos / van. A + el contracts to al. Ir a + infinitive expresses an intended or approaching action. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Seeing and watching
lessons.objective: Seeing and watching: Ver commonly means see or watch; mirar emphasizes looking.

words.es: Veo las montañas desde mi ventana.
words.en: I see the mountains from my window.
Do you see the blue building?

words.es: Vemos a nuestros amigos los viernes.
words.en: We see our friends on Fridays.

words.es: Ellos ven el mapa en el teléfono.
words.en: They look at the map on the phone.

words.es: No veo bien sin mis lentes.
words.en: I cannot see well without my glasses.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing seeing and watching. Ver commonly means see or watch; mirar emphasizes looking. Present veo and participle visto are irregular; preterite vi and vio have no written accent. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Giving and fixed expressions
lessons.objective: Giving and fixed expressions: Dar gives something to a recipient: le doy el libro.

words.es: Doy mi número a una compañera.
words.en: I give my number to a classmate.
She gives me a sheet of paper.
Will you give me a glass of water?

words.es: Mis vecinos dan un paseo por la tarde.
words.en: My neighbors go for a walk in the afternoon.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing giving and fixed expressions. Dar gives something to a recipient: le doy el libro. Doy is the irregular present yo form. Dar una vuelta means go for a walk or ride. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Knowing information and skills
lessons.objective: Knowing information and skills: Saber + infinitive means know how to do something.

words.es: Sé la dirección de la escuela.
words.en: I know the address of the school.
My sister knows how to swim.

words.es: No sabemos a qué hora empieza la clase.
words.en: We do not know what time the class begins.
Do you know where the stop is?
They know how to make this soup.

words.es: Ahora sé cómo llegar al centro.
words.en: Now I know how to get downtown.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing knowing information and skills. Saber + infinitive means know how to do something. Saber a fact contrasts with conocer a person or place. Present yo is sé, with an accent. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.
